messages:
anna_finance: Heads up — billing policy update going live next quarter. We're deprecating the legacy free-credit top-up and introducing a sliding burst window to smooth short-term overage volatility. Please read and surface to your teams.

billing-bot: Policy summary: legacy_free_credit deprecation + sliding_burst_window rollout. Effective 2026-05-01 for Hosted. See internal KB link.

mike_prod: Can you clarify what customers will actually see on invoices? Trying to anticipate support tickets.

anna_finance: Invoices will include a new line item called "Burst smoothing adjustment" when applicable. We're also issuing a one-time conversion credit for remaining legacy free credits; customers can opt into a new small-business credit program instead.

leah_support: Request: sample email/canned reply for customers surprised by converted credit amounts. Also need an internal triage doc for escalations.

anna_finance: Draft canned replies are in the KB draft link. Short message: no retroactive punitive charges, conversion formula shown in Console -> Billing -> Credit preview. Escalations should route to billing@redwood with subject prefix [Billing-Convert].

billings-bot: Note: customers with active Dedicated contracts are exempt from automatic migration; sales must request migration.

mike_prod: Will rate limiting behavior (429s) change? We had integration breakage last quarter from strict backoff logic.

anna_finance: No change to 429 semantics. Sliding burst window only affects accounting for short bursts and how temporary allowances are calculated for billing. SDK guidance will include recommended retry/backoff patterns.

annie_sre: What telemetry will be emitted so eng teams can monitor?

anna_finance: New response headers: X-Redwood-BurstWindow (current window percentile) and X-Redwood-SmoothingFactor. Meter events: burst_window_open, burst_window_close, burst_smoothing_applied. Console dashboards under Billing -> Burst analytics will be available.

annie_sre: I'll add smoke tests to assert headers and create an alert if smoothing adjustments exceed 25% for top 50 customers.

anna_finance: Rollout timeline: 2026-05-01 opt-in tests (small percentage of Hosted); 2026-06-01 default for new customers; 2026-07-01 global default for legacy Hosted with 30-day opt-out. Dedications unchanged unless opted in.

leah_support: I'll post KB and canned replies by 2026-04-21 and notify #sales and #customer-success.

sam_ceo: Thanks team. Keep customer communications empathetic and clear. Consider an opt-out email for the first month post-migration to avoid churn.

anna_finance: Agreed. We'll implement explicit opt-out for 30 days and email notice. Legal has approved the customer notice.

billing-bot: Links: internal doc https://redwood.example/internal/billing/sliding-burst; KB draft https://redwood.example/drafts/billing/smoothing.

mike_prod: One last ask: will Console reporting include both raw token counts and billing-adjusted totals? Some customers rely on raw for budgeting.

anna_finance: Yes 026-05 Console will show both raw usage and billing-adjusted columns with a toggle.

leah_support: Draft posted for review: https://redwood.example/drafts/support-burst-smoothing. Ping me for wording suggestions.

anna_finance: Action list: support to publish KB (leah_support by 2026-04-21), eng-runtime to emit headers/events (diane_sre by 2026-04-25), sales to outreach affected customers (sales ops by 2026-04-22), finance to update invoice template (anna_finance by 2026-05-01).

sam_ceo: Appreciate the coordinated plan. Keep me posted if we see unexpected churn signals.

billing-bot: End of thread.
